description: WHAT A THING IS SUPPOSED TO COST — per bin, per acre, per hour — for a date range. The other half of a variance: an actual with nothing to compare it against is a number, and the comparison is the control. DATED RATHER THAN A VALUE ON AN ITEM, because costs move every season and a variance computed against the wrong season's standard is a confident wrong number, which is worse than no variance. Two standards for one subject and basis may not overlap.

fields.description: What this is the standard cost OF — an item code, or the name of an activity: 'HARVEST-GALA', 'Hand thinning', 'Packing line hour'. FREE TEXT RATHER THAN A LINK, deliberately: half of what a farm wants a standard for is an activity that is not an Item on anybody's site, and forcing 'hand thinning' to become an Item to be costed would put a row in the stock module that has no business there.
fields.label: Subject

fields.description: The denominator. Part of the identity: a standard per acre and a standard per bin for the same activity are two different standards and may both be live.
fields.label: Basis
fields.options:
Per Unit
Per Acre
Per Hour
Per Bin
Per Box
Per Ton

fields.description: First day this standard applies, INCLUSIVE.
fields.label: Effective From

fields.description: Last day it applies, INCLUSIVE. BLANK MEANS OPEN-ENDED, which is the normal shape — a standard set this season and not yet superseded. Closing one is how a new season's standard is made without an overlap.
fields.label: Effective To

fields.description: Which pool this belongs to, so a variance report can group by it. A variance of nine thousand dollars is a fact; nine thousand dollars OF LABOR is a finding somebody can act on.
fields.label: Category
fields.options:
Labor
Materials
Machinery
Overhead
Packing
Storage
Freight
Other

fields.description: Where actuals for this subject accumulate. It is what lets get_cost_variance_report read the actual side out of the ledger instead of being told it.
fields.label: Cost Center

fields.description: The GL account actuals for this subject land in. With this and a cost center the actual side is computable; with neither, the report says so rather than reporting zero — a variance against an actual of zero would flag every standard on the site as massively under budget.
fields.label: Account

fields.description: How far actual may drift from standard before the `cost_variance` control has an opinion. PER STANDARD rather than one site-wide number, because a fuel standard and a labor standard do not deserve the same band — and a single tolerance that fits neither is how a variance report becomes noise.
fields.label: Tolerance %

fields.description: Where this number came from — 'three-year average', '2026 grower contract'. A standard nobody can source is a standard nobody defends when the variance is large.
fields.label: Notes

name: Standard Cost
